Loopback to spec-writer: Naming contract met (R2, R3, S1-S3): the six assets exist in assets/. player.glb has six separate parts: torso, head, arm_left, arm_right, leg_left and leg_right. Each other asset has a node with its contracted name.; Dimensions and look match the spec: ground block 2x2x1, platform 2x1.2x0.4, spike about 0.8 tall, coin disc of radius 0.3 with its faces along Z, pole 2.2 tall with a triangular flag, player 1.8 tall with limb pivots at the top ends. The palette is built with bpy Principled BSDF only.; Pipeline matches the spec: build_all.py is the single entry point. render_lineup.py reuses the same build() functions with no importer, and renders with Cycles on CPU at 32 samples (at most 64) and 960x540. It creates assets/ and evidence/ if missing, and paths are relative to the repo root.; S6 holds: blender/ has no import_scene, image.load or bpy.data.images.load, and no binary or bytecode files. `npm test` passes 6/6 (S1-S6). The lineup render shows all six assets in a row.; Non-blocking: R4 (determinism) has no test of its own. The tests check node names only, not dimensions or materials, so those were verified by reading the code and the render.; Review file written to reviews/wo-gh-1-reviewer-spec.md.; No network access, subprocess, eval/exec or dynamic imports in blender/*.py or tests/asset-factory.test.js. The scripts import only bpy, mathutils, the stdlib (sys, pathlib, math) and sibling modules, so no external assets are loaded (spec S6).; File writes go only to ROOT/assets and ROOT/evidence, with fixed names derived from module names. No user-controlled paths.; package.json: only the test glob changed, to "tests/**/*.test.js". It adds no dependencies and no install scripts.; Minor, non-blocking: build_all.py puts the blender/ directory first on sys.path, so a future file named like a stdlib module would shadow it. No current filename collides.; The review is written to reviews/wo-gh-1-reviewer-security.md. I did not run the scripts or tests; this is a static read of the code.; `npm test` ran 6 tests (S1 to S6): 6 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. Each test is named for its spec scenario.; S1 to S4 parse the real glb header and JSON chunk (magic, length, chunk type) from assets/*.glb. They check the six player part names (exactly one node each), the node name of each of the other five assets, and the 800 B to 5 MB size bounds.; S5 checks the PNG signature and the IHDR width and height (960x540) of evidence/asset-lineup.png. S6 scans every file under blender/ for import_scene, image.load and bpy.data.images.load, and rejects binary files.; Non-blocking gaps: S3 does not check that the named node is the only one. R4 determinism and the Cycles/64-sample limit have no tests, and the spec does not require any. A stray __pycache__ under blender/ would fail S6.; The review is written to reviews/wo-gh-1-reviewer-tests.md.; The code fits the standing decisions in brain/project.md. There is one module per asset, with blender/build_all.py as the single entry point. render_lineup.py reuses build_all.ASSETS. Only primitives and procedural materials are used. The player is six named parts. Tests parse the glb files without Blender. There is no importer or image loader anywhere in blender/.; The approved contract was edited inside the feature change. .openspec/specs/asset-factory/spec.md is modified in the working tree. Its status changed from 'approved for build' to 'revised, awaiting approval'. The character look line and the render_lineup.py import clause were also rewritten. The builder and reviewer stations do not own the spec, so the code is now built against a spec that is no longer approved. Either re-approve the revised spec at the spec-writer stage or the human gate, or revert the edit and fit the code to the approved text.; package.json changes the test script from 'node --test tests/' to 'node --test "tests/**/*.test.js"'. The change is reasonable, but the spec and work order do not mention it. Record it.; The project has no brain/decisions directory. The only decision file is .anvil-factory/brain/decisions/0001-composable-stations.md, which concerns ANVIL stations and does not apply to the asset code. The review used the standing decisions in brain/project.md instead. I did not run Blender 4.5.15 in this station.; The review is written to reviews/wo-gh-1-reviewer-architecture.md.; No design system exists for this project. The project must define design/DESIGN.md and design/tokens.json before interface output can be reviewed against design standards.
